transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I came in today because... people have actually been noticing how I'm moving lately. It's kind of two extremes. Sometimes it's like I'm moving underwater, you know? It takes me forever just to answer a question or even get out of a chair. 

But then other times, it's the opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together like I'm trying to shake off a bad call from work. It's getting pretty obvious to people, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Along with these changes in how you move, have you noticed any significant shifts in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other end, unusually elated or irritable?

Not really, no. I haven't noticed any big changes with my mood like that. I don't feel unusually sad or hopeless... and I'm definitely not feeling super elated or irritable either. As far as I can tell, it's really just been the physical stuff I mentioned, the moving too slow or pacing around, that's been the issue.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started or changed the dose of, any antipsychotic medications or other psychiatric drugs?
No, I'm not taking any medications like that. I haven't started anything new or changed any doses recently. I don't take any psychiatric drugs at all right now.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others find strange or hard to believe?

Actually, yes, I have noticed some things like that. Um, I work in customer service, and sometimes I’ll hear my old headset beep. Or... I'll hear a voice that sounds like a supervisor saying my name, or telling me I'm "too slow." 

But the thing is, my laptop will be completely closed, and there’s no phone ringing anywhere in the apartment. So, yeah, I guess I am hearing sounds and voices that aren't actually there.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or been diagnosed with any neurological or metabolic conditions around the time these symptoms started?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick lately, no head injuries... and I haven't been diagnosed with any medical conditions or anything. I've been physically healthy, as far as I know.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of slowed movement, pacing, and hearing these voices or sounds — days, weeks, or longer?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say about... two years and three months. It all started right after I got fired from my customer support job.
During these episodes of slowed movement, do you ever find yourself unable to speak at all, holding unusual body positions for a long time, or resisting when someone tries to move your arms or legs?

No, I don't think I've ever been completely unable to speak, or... had anyone try to move my arms and I resisted. It's not quite like that. 

But I do get kind of stuck sometimes. Like, when I get really overwhelmed, I'll sometimes catch myself just standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth, just frozen there for a bit. Or... I'll realize I'm walking the same little loop by the couch over and over for no real reason. So I do get stuck in positions or do repetitive things, just maybe not exactly in the way you described.
Over these past two years, how have these episodes affected your ability to work, maintain relationships, or take care of your daily responsibilities?

Well, I can still keep a roof over my head, so I'm getting by, I guess. But... I've really lost momentum with steady work. I end up missing deadlines or avoiding calls, and I know I come across as unreliable to employers. 

As for relationships, I definitely see my friends a lot less than I used to. I just kind of isolate. And daily stuff... basic routines like making meals, running errands, or even going hiking like I used to enjoy... I just let all that slide unless I really force myself to do it. It's just hard to keep up with everything.
